statements.quote: Headache pills—particularly those containing acetaminophen (also known as paracetamol or Tylenol) or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen—can cause liver damage

source.title: Headache pills and the liver (Google AI Overview)

statements.quote: In large amounts, NAPQI builds up and causes oxidative stress, leading to sudden (acute) liver injury or failure.

source.title: Headache pills and the liver (Google AI Overview)

statements.frequency_phrase: usually when taken in excess, combined with alcohol, or used long-term
statements.note: Drinking alcohol makes lower doses harmful. Acetaminophen is an active ingredient in more than 600 other medicines (cold, flu, sinus), so a hidden double dose is easy.

statements.quote: Acetaminophen, sold to the American consumer as Tylenol, is the single largest cause of acute liver failure in the United States. It is responsible for nearly fifty percent of all reported cases. It kills approximately five hundred Americans every year.

source.title: Mad Honey, chapter 4: the pharmaceutical machine (Nir Strulovitz)
